plain: The story is that Nazi Germany built a secret bell-shaped machine, called Die Glocke (German for "the Bell"), that spun mercury and may have been an attempt at anti-gravity. Much of it traces to Igor Witkowski, a Polish journalist, and the defence writer Nick Cook says Witkowski told him the whole Bell story in person, adding the codename "Kronos" and a site at Waldenburg. Michels tells it in several episodes: he names the SS officer Hans Kammler as its head, says the SS medical chief Ernst Grawitz and the physicist Walther Gerlach reportedly worked on it, and says an SS officer named Jacob Spornberg documented "magnetic field separation, vortex compression"; once he frames it as a rumoured time-slowing project in a Nazi "wonder weapon" programme. Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, says he has read Witkowski's books and those of the writer Joseph Farrell on it, and Michels later says McConnell and Cook raised it and that he thinks the Bell is "no longer fictional". If true, the Nazis would have been working on a way to defeat gravity.
